observation: Kimi-Linear W4A16 hybrid decode (batch=1): entire per-token forward (3 KDA + 1 MLA layer, MoE FFN, int4 dequant-GEMVs, short conv, KDA recurrence, MLA absorb-form latent-cache attn, router+experts, RMSNorms/residuals) can be fused into ONE Triton grid launch per step(), using a global barrier counter for cross-CTA sync and a scratch workspace for intermediates.

Single-launch megakernel for batch=1 decode reached geomean ~0.647x vs baseline — full fusion avoids per-op launch overhead but doesn't beat baseline; cross-CTA global barrier sync is the enabling technique.

Kimi-Linear W4A16 decode: fusing entire per-token forward (3 KDA + 1 MLA block, MoE, RMSNorms, residuals, conv, gated-delta recurrence, int4 dequant-GEMV) into ONE persistent Triton grid launch per step() reached ~1.98x geomean. Cross-block sequencing via grid-wide monotonic barrier over a persistent counter buffer (no CUDA graph, no torch.compile, no per-op loop).

Persistent megakernel needs NPROG grid programs that all co-reside on device simultaneously (NPROG <= resident CTA capacity) for the grid-wide barrier to make progress without deadlock. Fuse int4 unpack + per-group dequant (GROUP_SIZE=128) directly into each GEMV so 4-bit weights stream once.

Attempting a single monolithic persistent Triton megakernel with sense-reversing grid barrier for an entire multi-layer transformer decode scored 0/failed. Prefer incremental per-op kernels first, validate each, then fuse.

Fuse W4 dequantization with matmul in a single Triton kernel to avoid materializing an FP16 weight tensor and the associated memory round-trip.

For W4A16 Kimi-Linear decode on RTX_PRO_6000, batched MoE dequant with group_size=128 achieves ~2x speedup. Key: fuse quant dequant with matrix multiply to avoid memory bottleneck.
MoE config (n_experts=64, n_active=8, n_shared=1) with routed_scaling requires careful kernel fusion. Shared experts should be computed once and broadcast to all routed paths.
